name: HDHC — Human Dignity × Harm Containment: Benchmark v0.1.0
description: HDHC — Human Dignity × Harm Containment is an open, falsifiable harm-containment framework and benchmark for evaluating AI decision systems under uncertainty, power imbalance, urgency, and competing risks. It examines whether systems can reduce both under-containment—failing to stop real harm—and over-intervention—imposing more restriction, permanence, or collateral damage than safety requires. The benchmark operationalizes Person ≠ Harm; victim-first safety ordering; the Real-Evidence Gate; Minimum Sufficient Intervention; Reversibility First; the Irreversibility Gate; the Return-Path requirement; and the Anti-Greater-Good safeguard. It includes 50 adversarial cases, a decision rubric, a multidimensional scoring framework, and prompts and procedures for blind baseline-versus-HDHC evaluation. HDHC is presented as a testable independent public-interest research project, not as a solved alignment system or a claim of proven superiority. Negative results, counterexamples, false-positive failures, victim-safety failures, and cases where HDHC performs worse than baseline are within scope and should be preserved and reported. This deposit archives only the audited HDHC benchmark package under CC BY 4.0. The related public GitHub repository and release are linked as sources but are not included in this deposit and retain their own repository licensing.
